definition: Of a flue or similar passage, to permit airflow associated with combustion.
example: The inspector reported that the chimney was drawing well.
distinctions: The verb describes airflow through the passage, not a picture of it. A report about draw alone does not describe every aspect of the appliance’s condition.

originalSense.definition: Of a duct, smoking implement, etc.: to allow air to be passed through it in order that combustion can occur.

definition: To take a pull on a cigarette, pipe or similar smoking implement.
example: In the construction draw on a pipe, draw refers to taking a pull on the smoking implement.
distinctions: The preposition introduces the implement; this is separate from draw on a source meaning use it for support or information.
usage: Intransitive smoking-related reading; with at or on.

originalSense.definition: Followed by at or on: to drag or suck deeply on a cigarette, pipe, or other smoking implement.

definition: Of people, to gather together around a person or place.
example: The children drew around the guide to listen.
distinctions: Around or about identifies the gathering place. The group comes together; no one needs to be making a picture.

originalSense.definition: Chiefly followed by about or around: of a group of people: to come together; to assemble, to congregate, to gather.

definition: To lengthen or stretch something.
example: The metal was drawn into a long, thin strip.
distinctions: This is physical elongation. Drawing out a conversation instead extends its duration.

originalSense.definition: To make (something) larger or longer; to elongate, to stretch.

definition: To flatten metal, commonly by hammering, in the construction draw out.
example: In the recorded metalworking use, draw out can describe flattening a piece of metal, often by hammering.
distinctions: This source use concerns shaping metal. It is distinct from drawing out a reply or withdrawing money.

originalSense.definition: Followed by out: to flatten (a piece of metal), usually by hammering.

definition: To form or reduce wire by pulling metal through a die or aperture.
example: The manufacturer draws wire through a series of dies.
distinctions: The metal passes through an opening and changes cross-section. Wire drawing is a manufacturing process, not a drawn diagram of a wire.

originalSense.definition: To make (wire) by pulling a rod or other piece of metal through one or more apertures; also, to stretch (a rod or other piece of metal) into a wire.

distinctionTask.prompt: Wire drawing shapes metal by pulling it through a _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The named manufacturing process changes the metal’s cross-section.

definition: To straighten straw for thatching by pulling it through the hands.
example: In thatching terminology, drawing straw means preparing it into a straight, aligned condition.
distinctions: This preparatory sense is distinct from drawing straws at random to decide who does something.

originalSense.definition: To make (straw straight for thatching by pulling it through the hands.

definition: To amount to a specified quantity or sum.
example: The source records an obsolete object-taking use of draw meaning amount to a quantity or sum.
distinctions: This historical numerical use is not a command to select a random number or withdraw that sum.

originalSense.definition: To amount to (a certain quantity or sum).

definition: To prolong the duration of something, in an obsolete bare-verb use.
example: The source marks this bare prolonging use obsolete; modern draw out can still mean prolong a discussion or event.
distinctions: Do not label the modern phrasal verb draw out obsolete merely because this separately recorded bare use is obsolete.
usage: Obsolete transitive reading; compare current draw out.

originalSense.definition: To extend the duration of (something); to prolong.

definition: To stretch a person on a rack as a historical punishment.
example: In a historical punishment account, draw can denote forced stretching on a rack.
distinctions: This is a distinct historical reading from dragging to execution or disembowelling.

originalSense.definition: To stretch (someone) on a rack as a form of punishment or torture.

definition: To become longer or stretched.
example: In this intransitive elongation use, the subject itself is stretched or lengthened.
distinctions: This is the non-object-taking counterpart of drawing material longer. It does not mean that the material makes a picture.

originalSense.definition: To be made larger or longer; to be elongated or stretched.

definition: To straighten thatching straw by pulling it through the hands, without a stated direct object.
example: The source also records an intransitive thatching use of draw for preparing straw straight.
distinctions: The activity is understood from the thatching context; this is separate from random selection by drawing straws.

originalSense.definition: To make straw straight for thatching by pulling it through the hands.

definition: Of a sail, to fill with wind and become taut.
example: The sail began to draw as the breeze strengthened.
distinctions: A drawing sail is filling and working in the wind. This differs from the archaic object-taking use draw a sail meaning hoist it.

originalSense.definition: Of a sail: to fill with wind and become taut.

definition: To amount to a quantity or sum, without a direct object.
example: The source separately records an obsolete intransitive amounting use of draw.
distinctions: This is the intransitive counterpart of the obsolete quantity use, rather than a modern drawing or withdrawal instruction.

originalSense.definition: To amount to a certain quantity or sum.

definition: To extend or spread over an area or through space.
example: In an obsolete spatial use, draw can mean spread or stretch over an area.
distinctions: This historical extension sense is different from moving steadily in a direction in a modern phrasal construction.

originalSense.definition: To extend in area or space; to spread, to stretch.

definition: To pull something out of a place or container.
example: She drew a letter from the envelope.
distinctions: This is physical extraction. It need not involve a random selection or drawing a conclusion.

originalSense.definition: To pull (something) out; to extract, to remove.

distinctionTask.prompt: “She drew a letter from the envelope” describes _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: From the envelope selects physical extraction.

definition: To extract a tooth.
example: In a dental narrative, to draw a tooth means to extract it.
distinctions: This formal or older dental expression is separate from drawing a picture of a tooth. It names the action rather than explaining a procedure.

originalSense.definition: To extract (a tooth); to pull.

definition: To extract juice, oil or another fluid from something.
example: The salt drew moisture out of the sliced vegetables.
distinctions: The verb names extraction; the mechanism depends on the materials and process. It does not universally imply suction or one particular physical mechanism.

originalSense.definition: To extract (juice, oil, or some other fluid) from something by osmosis, pressure, or another process.

definition: To extract a small fluid sample, especially blood.
example: The nurse drew a blood sample for the test.
distinctions: This sample-taking use is distinct from a blow drawing blood and from drawing an anatomical picture. The vocabulary does not specify one sampling method.

originalSense.definition: To extract (a small amount of liquid, especially blood) by puncturing a surface, or by using a pipette, syringe, or other suction device.

distinctionTask.prompt: A nurse who draws a blood sample _____ it for testing.
distinctionTask.explanation: Draw a sample means obtain a specimen.

definition: To let tea infuse in water.
example: The source records an object-taking use of draw for allowing tea to infuse.
distinctions: This brewing sense is separate from pouring tea from a pot. Let the tea draw is the related intransitive construction.

originalSense.definition: To leave (tea) temporarily in water to allow the flavour to increase; to infuse, to steep.

definition: To pull a weapon from its holder or sheath.
example: The actor drew a sword during the scene.
distinctions: The object is taken out, rather than depicted in a picture. The context may be a staged performance rather than a real conflict.

originalSense.definition: To pull out (a firearm, sword, or other weapon) from a holster, sheath, etc.; to unsheathe.

definition: To take a beverage from a cask or keg using a pump or tap.
example: In a serving context, drawing a beverage takes it from a cask or keg.
distinctions: This use describes serving or extraction, not necessarily drinking the beverage.

originalSense.definition: To take (a beverage) from a cask or keg using a pump or tap; to tap.

definition: To take water from a well or other source.
example: They drew water from the well.
distinctions: Water is obtained from the source, for example by lifting or pumping. The verb does not identify one universal mechanism.

originalSense.definition: To take up (water) from a well or other source, especially by lifting in a container or pumping.

distinctionTask.prompt: To draw water from a well is to _____ it.
distinctionTask.explanation: The source context selects water extraction.

definition: To absorb liquid or nutrients, especially through a plant’s roots.
example: The roots draw water from the soil.
distinctions: This is uptake from the surroundings, not making a picture of the roots. Different substances and conditions involve different uptake processes.

originalSense.definition: To soak up (a liquid, etc.); to absorb; specifically, of an organism (especially a plant) or one of its parts: to take in (nutrients, water, etc.).

definition: Of a channel or drain, to carry water away.
example: The drain draws water away from the courtyard.
distinctions: The drainage context concerns removal of water, rather than drinking, picture-making or a random selection.

originalSense.definition: Of a channel, drain, etc.: to carry (water) away.

definition: To disembowel a person, in a historical punishment use.
example: In the recorded execution terminology, drawn can refer to disembowelling, particularly in accounts of hanging, drawing and quartering.
distinctions: Other branches of draw separately record dragging to execution and tearing apart. Do not infer one reading solely from the spelling drawn.

originalSense.definition: Chiefly in draw and quarter and hang, draw and quarter: to disembowel (someone), especially after hanging as a punishment for high treason.

definition: To remove an animal’s internal organs before cooking.
example: In older food-preparation terminology, drawing a bird means removing its internal organs.
distinctions: This culinary sense is separate from attracting birds and from drawing their pictures.

originalSense.definition: To remove the viscera from (an animal, especially a bird) before cooking.

definition: To bring bodily material towards the surface for removal, in historical medicine.
example: The source records draw in an older medical theory of attracting humours or pus towards the body’s surface.
distinctions: This reading reflects historical medical terminology and theory. It should not be read as a general modern explanation of how wounds are treated.

originalSense.definition: To attract (humours, pus, etc.), chiefly by bringing to the surface of the body, so it can be dispersed or removed; also, to treat (a wound) in this way.

definition: To raise coal or ore from an underground mine to the surface.
example: In mining terminology, drawing ore brings it from underground to the surface.
distinctions: This is extraction or hoisting, not a geological sketch or a lottery selection.

originalSense.definition: To raise (coal or ore) from an underground mine to the surface.

definition: To select one or more items from a collection by a random or chance procedure.
example: Each participant drew one numbered ticket from the bag.
distinctions: A draw selects an item or person. The word alone does not guarantee uniform chances or a fair procedure.

originalSense.definition: To select (one or more things) at random from a collection of similar things to decide which of a group of people will receive something such as a prize, or undergo something such as an assignment; also, to select (someone) by this process; to win (a prize) in a lottery or lucky draw.

distinctionTask.prompt: A lottery draw _____ guarantee equal chances without regard to procedure.
distinctionTask.explanation: The actual selection procedure determines the probabilities.

definition: To conduct a lottery selection or select its winning numbers or tickets.
example: The winning numbers will be drawn at noon.
distinctions: This use determines the lottery result. It is separate from describing a match with no winner.

originalSense.definition: To conduct, or select the winning numbers, tickets, etc., for, (a lottery).

definition: To empty the contents of a kiln, oven or similar enclosure.
example: In kiln terminology, drawing the kiln means removing its contents.
distinctions: The kiln or oven is the object of this emptying use, unlike draw a kiln meaning sketch its appearance.

originalSense.definition: To remove the contents of (something, especially a kiln or oven); to empty.

definition: To fill a bathtub with water for a bath.
example: She drew a bath for the child.
distinctions: Draw a bath means prepare its water, rather than make a picture of the bathtub.

originalSense.definition: To fill a bathtub with (water for a bath); to run (a bath).

distinctionTask.prompt: To draw a bath is to _____ it with water.
distinctionTask.explanation: The household expression means prepare the bathwater.

definition: To withdraw something, such as a bet or a horse from a race.
example: The source records archaic draw for withdrawing a wager or withdrawing a horse from a race.
collocations: draw a horse from a race (archaic)
distinctions: Withdraw is clearer in ordinary modern writing. This older use is separate from allocating the horse’s starting draw.

originalSense.definition: To withdraw (something); specifically , to withdraw (a bet or wager); also , to withdraw (a horse) from a race.

definition: Of plants or roots, to deplete soil of nutrients.
example: In the recorded regional agricultural sense, drawing soil emphasises depletion of its nutrients.
distinctions: This source use emphasises the effect on the soil, rather than merely naming neutral absorption by the plant. It does not assert that every uptake event leaves soil depleted.

originalSense.definition: Of a plant or its roots: to deplete (soil) of nutrients.

definition: To separate selected sheep from a flock for a particular purpose.
example: The farmer drew the lambs from the flock for sale.
distinctions: This agricultural use selects and separates animals. It is distinct from sketching the flock or necessarily selecting animals at random.

originalSense.definition: To separate (sheep) from a flock for a particular purpose, such as breeding or selling.

definition: To take or be dealt a playing card from a deck.
example: He drew a card from the top of the deck.
distinctions: Drawing obtains a card. Discarding removes one from a hand, and the game’s rules determine whether and how either action is available.

originalSense.definition: To be dealt or to take (a playing card) from the deck; also, to have (a particular hand) as a result of this.

distinctionTask.prompt: In a card game, drawing a card is _____ discarding one.
distinctionTask.explanation: Drawing obtains a card; discarding removes one from the hand.

definition: To fish an area of water by dragging a net along or through it.
example: In the source’s fishing use, drawing a stretch of water means working it with a dragged net.
collocations: draw a shore with a net
distinctions: Here the water area is the object, rather than the net itself in draw in the net.

originalSense.definition: To fish by dragging a fishing net along (a shore) or in (a body of water).

definition: To search a wood or covert for game.
example: In hunting terminology, drawing a covert means searching it for quarry.
distinctions: The place is searched, not sketched. This meaning is separate from drawing a weapon.

originalSense.definition: To search (a covert, a wood, etc.) for game or a quarry.

definition: To finish a game or match with neither side winning.
example: The two teams drew the league match one–one.
distinctions: The sport’s rules determine the result. A cricket draw can differ from both an equal score and a tie.

originalSense.definition: To end (a game or match) with neither side winning, that is, in a draw.

definition: To finish a timed cricket match without a win or tie because the required innings are not completed.
example: A two-innings cricket match can be drawn when time ends without a winning result, even if the teams’ totals are unequal.
distinctions: A cricket draw is different from a tie. The usual tie requires completed innings and equal scores; a draw need not have equal totals.

originalSense.definition: In a match scheduled to last for a certain period of time: to end (a match) with neither side winning because the team batting last has not completed its innings when the playing time concludes.

definition: To separate lengths of machine-made lace by removing connecting threads.
example: In historical lace manufacture, drawing separates sections joined during production.
distinctions: This industrial use is different from pulling on a lace that fastens clothing.

originalSense.definition: To separate (a length of lace made by machine) into sections by removing the threads connecting the sections.

definition: To milk a cow, in a northern Scottish use.
example: The source records draw a cow as a northern Scottish expression meaning milk the cow.
distinctions: This regional verb does not mean sketching the animal. Milk is the ordinary general English verb.

originalSense.definition: To take milk from (a cow); to milk.

definition: To separate clover or trefoil seeds from their husks.
example: The source records an obsolete agricultural use of draw for separating clover or trefoil seeds from husks.
distinctions: This specific historical processing use differs from sowing seeds or selecting them at random.

originalSense.definition: To separate (seeds) from the husks of clover or trefoil; also, to separate seeds from the husks of (clover or trefoil).

definition: To take a wicket, in a rare obsolete cricket use.
example: The source records a rare obsolete cricket use of draw meaning take a wicket.
distinctions: This is not the current match-result sense of drawing a cricket match.

originalSense.definition: To take (a wicket).

definition: To remove a hawk from its mew after moulting.
example: In the recorded falconry use, drawing a hawk removes it from its mew after it has moulted.
collocations: draw a hawk from the mew
distinctions: The hawk is the object of this specialised historical use. It is distinct from attracting a wild bird.

originalSense.definition: To remove (a hawk) from a mew after it has moulted.

definition: To steal, particularly by pickpocketing, in historical thieves’ slang.
example: The source records draw in obsolete thieves’ cant for stealing from a person or place.
distinctions: This is historical slang for theft, not ordinary drawing from one’s own bank account.

originalSense.definition: To steal (something) from a person, especially by picking a pocket; also to pick the pocket of (someone); to steal from (a place).

definition: To consume or take electrical power.
example: The heater draws two kilowatts while running.
distinctions: Kilowatts measure power; kilowatt-hours measure energy. At a constant 2 kW for one hour, the energy is 2 kWh. The example is not a measured appliance specification.

originalSense.definition: To consume (power).

distinctionTask.prompt: At a constant draw of 2 kW for one hour, energy used is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Power multiplied by duration gives energy; kW and kWh are different quantities.

definition: To obtain or elicit something.
example: The source uses this broad entry to introduce obtaining information, eliciting a response, inferring a conclusion and receiving money.
distinctions: Choose the specific child meaning for the actual context; obtaining a conclusion differs from physically withdrawing money.
usage: Broad lexical umbrella; specific children listed separately.

originalSense.definition: To obtain, elicit.

definition: To derive material or information from a source.
example: The report draws its evidence from interviews.
distinctions: From identifies the origin of the material. The quality of a source is a separate question from whether the report uses it.

originalSense.definition: To take (something) from a particular source, especially of information; to derive.

distinctionTask.prompt: “The report draws evidence from interviews” identifies the evidence’s _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: From identifies origin without independently proving quality.

definition: To elicit a response or statement from someone.
example: The question drew an honest answer from her.
distinctions: The response is brought forth, not necessarily deduced as a conclusion or quoted from a document.

originalSense.definition: To call forth (something) from a person, to elicit.

definition: To infer or reach a conclusion from information.
example: We drew a cautious conclusion from the results.
distinctions: Drawing a conclusion describes making an inference. Its justification depends on the evidence and reasoning; the verb alone does not make it proven.

originalSense.definition: To deduce or infer (a conclusion); to make (a deduction).

distinctionTask.prompt: To draw a conclusion is to make an _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: A conclusion’s strength depends on its supporting evidence and reasoning.

definition: To receive pay or withdraw money from an account.
example: She draws a salary from the college.
distinctions: Receiving a salary and withdrawing money are related money-obtaining uses, but salary receipt does not require physically taking cash from a bank.

originalSense.definition: To receive (a salary); to withdraw (money) from a bank etc.

distinctionTask.prompt: A person who draws a salary _____ pay.
distinctionTask.explanation: The financial context selects receipt of pay.

definition: To induce someone to speak or provide information on a subject.
example: She declined to be drawn on the proposed merger.
distinctions: The passive phrase means be induced to discuss the topic. Draw someone out is a related way to encourage them to speak more freely.

originalSense.definition: To elicit information from (someone); to induce (a person) to speak on some subject. (Now frequently in passive.)

distinctionTask.prompt: Someone who declines to be drawn on a topic refuses to be induced to _____ it.
distinctionTask.explanation: This passive construction concerns providing comments or information.

definition: To take a weapon from its holder, without a stated direct object.
example: In the duel scene, both actors drew.
distinctions: The weapon is understood from context rather than stated as a direct object. This is distinct from making a picture or drawing a card.

originalSense.definition: To pull out a firearm, sword, or other weapon from a holster, sheath, etc.

definition: To take water from a well or source, without a stated direct object.
example: In a well-side account, draw can stand without an object when taking water is understood.
distinctions: The unstated thing obtained is water. This is separate from an audience attraction that draws well.

originalSense.definition: To take up water from a well or other source, especially by lifting it in a container or pumping it.

definition: To make a chance selection without stating the selected item as a direct object.
example: We mixed the numbered tickets, and then it was my turn to draw.
distinctions: The tickets or other items are understood from context. The selection method determines the chances; draw alone does not guarantee fairness.

originalSense.definition: To select one or more things at random from a collection of similar things to decide which of a group of people will receive or undergo something.

definition: Of tea, to infuse; of a pot, to allow tea to infuse.
example: Let the tea draw before you pour it.
distinctions: Tea drawing concerns infusion, not pouring it out or making a picture. The desired time depends on the tea and preparation.

originalSense.definition: To leave tea temporarily in water to allow the flavour to increase; to infuse, to steep; also, of a teapot: to cause tea to infuse.

distinctionTask.prompt: Tea that is drawing is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The brewing use concerns contact with water and developing flavour.

definition: Of a bath, to be filled with water.
example: The source records a bath drawing as a bath being filled with water.
distinctions: The bath is the subject of this recorded use, unlike someone drawing a bath in the transitive construction.

originalSense.definition: Of a bathtub: to be filled with water for a bath; to be run.

definition: Of a channel or drain, to carry water away without a stated direct object.
example: In the recorded intransitive drainage use, a channel that draws carries water away.
distinctions: Water is understood from the drainage context. The subject does not make an illustration.

originalSense.definition: Of a channel, drain, etc.: to carry water away.

definition: Of a liquid, to drain away or percolate.
example: In this recorded liquid-movement use, the liquid draws by draining or percolating away.
distinctions: The liquid is the moving subject, unlike a drain drawing water away. This does not mean the liquid necessarily evaporates.

originalSense.definition: Of a liquid: to drain away, to percolate.

definition: To treat a wound by attracting material towards the surface, in historical medicine.
example: The source also records an intransitive version of the older medical drawing use associated with humours or pus.
distinctions: This is historical vocabulary, separate from the current medical term draw blood for taking a sample.

originalSense.definition: To treat a wound by attracting humours, pus, etc., chiefly by bringing such material to the surface of the body, so it can be dispersed or removed.

definition: To take a playing card, without stating it as a direct object.
example: The rules allow each player to draw before discarding.
distinctions: The card is understood from context. The example describes a particular rule, not a rule followed by every card game.

originalSense.definition: To be dealt or to take a playing card from the deck.

definition: To take a domino from the stock.
example: In this drawing game, she could not play, so she drew.
distinctions: The action depends on the variant: not every domino game allows drawing, and the number permitted is rule-dependent.

originalSense.definition: To take a domino from the stock.

definition: To end a match with neither side winning, without a direct object.
example: The teams drew one–one in the league.
distinctions: No match is named as a direct object in this construction. The relevant sport and rules determine what counts as a draw.

originalSense.definition: To end a game or match with neither side winning, that is, in a draw; to tie.

definition: To serve drinks from casks or kegs, in an obsolete tavern-work use.
example: In an older inn account, a person who draws works at serving drink from casks or kegs.
distinctions: This occupational use means serve drink, not necessarily consume it. It is separate from draw meaning take a swig.

originalSense.definition: To take alcoholic beverages from casks or kegs in an inn or tavern; to work as a drawer or barman.

definition: To remove a hawk from its mew after moulting, without a stated direct object.
example: The source separately records intransitive draw for the falconry activity of removing a hawk from its mew after moulting.
distinctions: The bird is understood rather than expressed as a direct object. This is a specialised historical activity, not ordinary picture-making.

originalSense.definition: To remove a hawk from a mew after it has moulted.

definition: To move oneself in a specified direction, in a now rare reflexive use.
example: The source records a rare reflexive use in which a person draws themself in a direction.
distinctions: The reflexive object names the moving person. The common modern train drew into the station instead has no reflexive object.

originalSense.definition: To move in a specific direction.

definition: To move steadily into a direction or position.
example: The train drew into the station.
distinctions: A preposition or adverb identifies the direction or position. The train is moving, not producing an image.

originalSense.definition: To move steadily in a particular direction or into a specific position.

distinctionTask.prompt: “The train drew into the station” describes _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The intransitive movement verb is followed by into and a destination.

definition: To approach a particular time or moment.
example: Evening drew near as we reached the village.
distinctions: The approach is temporal in this context. Draw to a close is a related construction for approaching an ending.

originalSense.definition: To come to, towards (a particular moment in time); to approach (a time).

distinctionTask.prompt: “Evening drew near” describes an approach in _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The event or time is approaching.

definition: To search for or track quarry.
example: In the source’s now rare hunting use, draw can mean search for game or track quarry.
distinctions: This intransitive tracking use is separate from searching a named covert as a direct object and from drawing a weapon.

originalSense.definition: To search for game; to track a quarry.

definition: To produce a picture, diagram or line with a pen, pencil or other instrument.
example: She drew a simple map to show the route.
distinctions: This picture-making use has a stated object. Draw a conclusion means infer, and draw a crowd means attract; neither requires a physical picture.

originalSense.definition: To produce (a figure, line, picture, representation of something, etc.) with a piece of chalk, a crayon, a pen, a pencil, or other instrument.

distinctionTask.prompt: She has _____ a map in her notebook.
distinctionTask.explanation: The past participle after has is drawn, not the simple past drew.

definition: To carve or shape an object by cutting off thin pieces.
example: The source records a shaping use of draw for removing thin pieces from an object.
distinctions: This specialised shaping use changes the object itself, rather than making a two-dimensional picture of it.

originalSense.definition: To carve or shape (something) by cutting off thin pieces.

definition: To make a comparison, contrast or distinction between things.
example: The author draws a comparison between urban and rural transport.
distinctions: A comparison examines a relationship and need not claim that the things are identical. A distinction identifies a relevant difference.

originalSense.definition: To make (a comparison or contrast) between two or more things; to compare; to contrast, to distinguish.

distinctionTask.prompt: To draw a comparison is to _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Comparing can identify both similarities and differences.

definition: To write a cheque, bill or draft authorising payment.
example: She drew a cheque on her bank.
collocations: a draft drawn on a bank
distinctions: The payment order is written or issued. This is different from withdrawing cash from an account, and the word does not by itself establish available funds.
usage: Financial-document verb; often with on or upon.

originalSense.definition: Often followed by on or upon and the person or institution providing the money: to write (a bill, cheque, or draft) to authorize payment of money.

definition: To compose a document, usually in the construction draw up.
example: The lawyers drew up a new agreement.
distinctions: Draw up means prepare or compose. Preparing an agreement does not by itself make it final, signed or legally effective.

originalSense.definition: Now chiefly in the form draw up: to compose or write (a piece of text, especially a formal document).

distinctionTask.prompt: To prepare an agreement, draw it _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Draw up is the document-preparation construction.

definition: To portray or describe something in words.
example: In a few sentences, she drew a vivid picture of village life.
distinctions: The representation is linguistic. No physical sketch or photograph is required by this figurative use.

originalSense.definition: To depict (something) linguistically; to portray (something) in words; to describe.

definition: To create a furrow by pulling a plough through soil.
example: The plough drew a straight furrow through the soil.
distinctions: The furrow is made in the soil, rather than merely represented in a farm plan.

originalSense.definition: To create (a furrow) by pulling a plough through soil.

definition: To devise or arrange something, in an obsolete use.
example: The source records draw as an obsolete verb for devising or arranging something.
distinctions: The modern phrasal verb draw up a plan is related but is not made obsolete by this historical bare-verb entry.

originalSense.definition: To arrange or devise (something); to contrive.

definition: To produce a three-dimensional model or sculpture.
example: The source records an obsolete modelling use of draw for making a three-dimensional figure.
distinctions: This historical sculptural meaning differs from the ordinary modern picture-making verb.

originalSense.definition: To produce (a three-dimensional figure of something); to model, to mould, to sculpt.

definition: To make pictures or drawings without naming a direct object.
example: She likes to draw in her sketchbook.
distinctions: No direct object is stated. She draws maps is the corresponding object-taking construction, while draws a salary is a different meaning.

originalSense.definition: To produce an image of something with a piece of chalk, a crayon, a pen, a pencil, or other instrument; to make a drawing or drawings.

distinctionTask.prompt: In “She likes to draw”, a direct object is _____.

originalSense.definition: In weft knitting, a single row of loops connecting the loops of the preceding and following rows.

originalSense.definition: A position in an arrangement, disposition, or sequence.

wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: The stewards restored _____ after the disturbance.

distinctionTask.prompt: We placed an _____ for two replacement parts.

example: Your order has been packed and is ready for collection.

originalSense.definition: The goods requested.
originalSense.example: Your order should arrive within two days.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: Your _____ has been packed and is ready to collect.
distinctionTask.explanation: Here order refers to the purchased goods.

definition: A religious community whose members follow a shared rule or principles.
example: She joined a religious order that runs schools.
distinctions: This names an organised religious community; holy orders instead concerns ordained ministry.

originalSense.definition: A group of religious adherents, especially monks or nuns, set apart within their religion by adherence to a particular rule or set of principles.
originalSense.example: St. Ignatius Loyola founded the Jesuit order in 1537.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: An association or body of knights.
example: The knight was admitted to the order.

originalSense.definition: An association of knights.
originalSense.example: the Order of the Garter, the Order of the Bath.

definition: A body of people united by a shared interest or profession.
example: A reference to an order of physicians uses order for a body of people sharing a profession.
distinctions: This reading names an organised body of people, rather than a command, purchase request or numerical sequence.

originalSense.definition: Any group of people with common interests.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: An honour or decoration awarded for distinguished service.
example: She was awarded the order for distinguished public service.
distinctions: An order can be a named honour with several grades; it is not necessarily a single generic medal or a command.

originalSense.definition: A decoration, awarded by a government, a dynastic house, or a religious body to an individual, usually for distinguished service to a nation or to humanity.

wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: A taxonomic rank below class and above family, or a taxon at that rank.
example: Magnolias are classified in the order Magnoliales.
distinctions: The rank is class, then order, then family. It differs from order as an arbitrary sorted sequence.

originalSense.definition: A category in the classification of organisms, ranking below class and above family; a taxon at that rank.
originalSense.example: The magnolia and nutmeg families belong to the order Magnoliales.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: In taxonomy, the rank between class and family is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Order is below class and above family.

definition: A rank, class, kind or level of people or things.
example: The problem requires mathematical skill of a high order.
distinctions: Of a high order can describe a high level of quality. Older references to orders of society concern social classes.

originalSense.definition: A number of things or persons arranged in a fixed or suitable place, or relative position; a rank; a row; a grade; especially, a rank or class in society; a distinct character, kind, or sort.
originalSense.example: the higher or lower orders of society
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: An ecclesiastical rank or ordained ministry, especially in holy orders.
example: He was admitted to holy orders.
distinctions: In this expression orders concerns ministry, rather than joining a monastic or religious community.

originalSense.definition: An ecclesiastical rank or position, usually for the sake of ministry, (especially, when plural) holy orders.
originalSense.example: There have been many major and minor orders in the history of Christianity: the order of virgins, of deacons, priests, lectors, acolytes, porters, catechists, widows, etc.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: A classical architectural system governing columns and the structure they support.
example: The facade uses the Doric order.
distinctions: An architectural order includes proportions and details of columns and entablature; it is more than their left-to-right arrangement.

originalSense.definition: The disposition of a column and its component parts, and of the entablature resting upon it, in classical architecture; hence (since the column and entablature are the characteristic features of classical architecture) a style or manner of architectural design.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: The sequence in which a cricket side’s batters bat.
example: The coach moved her up the batting order.
distinctions: This is a place in the team’s batting sequence, rather than the final score or a command to bat.

originalSense.definition: The sequence in which a side’s batsmen bat; the batting order.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: A scale, size or scope used in comparison.
example: The new project involves costs of a different order.
distinctions: The general scale sense need not specify an exact ratio. A difference of one order of magnitude usually means a factor of ten.
usage: Sciences, engineering and comparisons of scale.

originalSense.definition: Scale: size or scope.
originalSense.example: on another order
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: The degree of a relevant polynomial or transfer function used to characterise an electronic circuit or filter.
example: The circuit uses a second-order low-pass filter.
distinctions: For a conventional all-pole low-pass filter, order is the degree of its transfer function’s denominator. It does not mean the stage’s position in a cascade.
usage: Electronics; the precise convention depends on the circuit model.

originalSense.definition: A power of polynomial function in an electronic circuit’s block, such as a filter, an amplifier, etc.
originalSense.example: a 3-stage cascade of a 2nd-order bandpass Butterworth filter
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: For a power-law rate expression, the sum of the concentration exponents; individual exponents give orders with respect to each species.
example: For rate = k[A]²[B], the overall order is three.
distinctions: Reaction orders are determined experimentally and may be fractional, negative or zero. They are generally not predictable from stoichiometric coefficients, and a rate law need not be a polynomial.
usage: Chemical kinetics; a stated power-law rate expression.

originalSense.definition: The overall power of the rate law of a chemical reaction, expressed as a polynomial function of concentrations of reactants and products.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: For rate = k[A]²[B], what is the overall reaction order? _____
distinctionTask.explanation: Add the concentration exponents 2 and 1. They describe this stated rate law.

definition: The number of elements of a set or algebraic structure.
example: The cyclic group has order four because it contains four elements.
collocations: a finite group of order four
distinctions: The order of a group counts all its elements. The order of one group element is the repetition count needed to reach the identity.

originalSense.definition: The number of elements contained within (the given object); formally, the cardinality (of the given object).
originalSense.example:
1911 [Cambridge University Press], William Burnside, Theory of Groups of Finite Order, 2nd Edition, Reprint, Dover (Dover Phoenix), 2004, page 222,
In this case, the conjugate set contains n(n − 1)/x(x − 1) distinct sub-groups of order m, and H is therefore self-conjugate in a group K of order x(x − l)m.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: A group contains six elements. What is its order? _____
distinctionTask.explanation: The order of the group is its cardinality, six; individual elements can have different orders.

definition: The least positive number of repetitions of a group element that gives the identity, if it exists.
example: In the rotational symmetry group of a square, a quarter-turn has order four.
distinctions: Four quarter-turns give the identity rotation. An element has infinite order if no positive power gives the identity; its order is not the number of all elements in the group.

originalSense.definition: The smallest positive natural number n such that (denoting the group operation multiplicatively) gⁿ is the identity element of G, if such an n exists; if no such n exists the element is said to be of infinite order (or sometimes zero order).
originalSense.example: The object of this note is to observe that it is possible to calculate the order of an element A of G#61;#92;mathit#123;GL#125;(d,q) on average using O(d³#92;mathsf#123;log#125;#92;q) field operations, assuming that qⁱ-1 has been factorised for i#92;led.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: A quarter-turn of a square first returns to the identity after four repetitions. Its order is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The order is the least positive repetition count giving the identity.

definition: The number of vertices in a graph.
example: The graph has order five because it has five vertices.
distinctions: Graph order counts vertices; graph size commonly counts edges. Neither describes the drawing’s physical dimensions.

originalSense.definition: The number of vertices in the graph (i.e. the set-theoretic order of the set of vertices of the graph).
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: A graph has five vertices and seven edges. Its order is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Graph order counts vertices, while size commonly counts edges.

definition: A set equipped with a partial-order relation.
example: In order-theory writing, a finite order can mean a set equipped with a partial-order relation.
distinctions: This use names the ordered structure. Another use of order names only its comparison relation; not every pair must be comparable.

originalSense.definition: A partially ordered set.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: The relation used to partially order a set.
example: Set inclusion defines an order on these subsets.
distinctions: A partial order is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive. It need not compare every pair; that additional condition gives a total order.

originalSense.definition: The relation with which a partially ordered set is equipped.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: The sum of a monomial’s variable exponents, also called its total degree.
example: The monomial x²y³z has order six.
distinctions: In x²y³z the exponents are 2, 3 and 1, so the total is 6. The coefficients are not included in that sum.

originalSense.definition: The sum of the exponents of the variables involved in the expression.
originalSense.example: The monomial x²ʸ³ᶻ is of order 2#43;3#43;1#61;6.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: The monomial x²y³z has total order _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Add the variable exponents 2 + 3 + 1.

definition: The largest variable exponent in a nonzero polynomial in one variable, also called its degree.
example: The polynomial 4x³ + x has order three.
distinctions: For one variable, inspect the highest power with a nonzero coefficient. Do not add the exponents of separate terms.

originalSense.definition: The order of the leading monomial; (equivalently) the largest power of the variable involved in the given expression.
originalSense.example: The quadratic polynomial ax²#43;bx#43;c, is said to be of order (or degree) 2 when a is nonzero.
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: The nonzero polynomial 4x³ + x has order _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The highest variable exponent is 3; the leading coefficient 4 does not give its degree.

definition: A written payment direction or instrument authorising someone to receive money or property.
example: The clerk issued a postal order for the amount due.
distinctions: This is a payment instrument or direction, rather than an order requesting goods from a supplier.

originalSense.definition: A written direction to furnish someone with money or property; compare money order, postal order.

definition: To put things into a specified sequence.

originalSense.definition: To set in some sort of order.

wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

definition: To arrange things in a proper or orderly state.

originalSense.definition: To arrange, set in proper order.
originalSense.example: The books in the shelf need ordering.

definition: To direct someone authoritatively to do something.

originalSense.definition: To issue a command to; to charge.
originalSense.example: to order troops to advance
wordFamily: Ancient and Honorable Order of Turtles

distinctionTask.prompt: The officer _____ the crowd to move back.
distinctionTask.explanation: Order someone to do something is the command construction.

definition: To request goods or services, especially as a purchase.
example: We ordered two coffees at the cafe.
distinctions: The thing requested is the object. An instruction to a person normally follows order someone to do something.

originalSense.definition: To request some product or service; to secure by placing an order.
originalSense.example: You can now order most products to be delivered to your home.

distinctionTask.prompt: We _____ two coffees from the cafe.
distinctionTask.explanation: Here ordered means requested to buy; ordained concerns admission to ministry.

originalSense.definition: To admit to holy orders; to ordain; to receive into the ranks of the ministry.

definition: A shortened name for the Order of the Arrow.

definition: (Older usage) A limit, boundary or endpoint.

definition: A condition or restriction attached to an agreement or arrangement.

originalSense.definition: A condition or restriction.

distinctionTask.explanation: Terms are the agreed conditions, which can concern more than timing.

definition: A period of time or a division of a longer period.

originalSense.definition: A chronological limitation or division.

distinctionTask.explanation: Term gives the period for which the agreement runs.

definition: The state of relations between people.

usage: Plural; chiefly in expressions such as on good terms.

originalSense.definition: Relations among people.

distinctionTask.explanation: On friendly terms describes their relationship.

definition: A meaningful unit, such as a word, expression or logical component.

originalSense.definition: A unit or component with a certain meaning.
originalSense.example: "Algorithm" is a term used in computer science.

originalSense.definition: An essential dignity in which unequal segments of every astrological sign have internal rulerships which affect the power and integrity of each planet in a natal chart.

originalSense.definition: A point, line, or superficies that limits.
originalSense.example: A line is the term of a superficies, and a superficies is the term of a solid.

originalSense.definition: A piece of carved work placed under each end of the taffrail.

definition: To call or describe something by a particular name or expression.
example: She termed the proposal a compromise.

originalSense.definition: To phrase a certain way; to name or call.

distinctionTask.prompt: She _____ the proposal a compromise.
distinctionTask.explanation: Termed means called or described; terminated means ended.

definition: (Medicine) Born or delivered at term.
example: The report distinguishes preterm and term infants.

originalSense.definition: Born or delivered at term.
originalSense.example: term neonate

definition: (Informal computing) A terminal-emulator program.

distinctions: This clipping refers to a program providing a terminal interface, rather than a technical word or time period.

originalSense.definition: A computer program that emulates a physical terminal.

definition: (Workplace slang) To terminate someone’s employment.
example: In workplace slang, term may shorten terminate and refer to ending employment.
distinctions: This informal clipping concerns the employment relationship; it does not mean naming the person or setting a contract duration.

originalSense.definition: To terminate someone's employment.

definition: (Moderation jargon) To delete or terminate someone’s account.
example: In moderation jargon, term can mean deleting or terminating an account.
distinctions: The object is an account in this sense. Ending a person’s employment is another use of the clipping.

originalSense.definition: To delete someone's account.

definition: (Workplace jargon) A person whose employment has been terminated.
example: As a noun in workplace jargon, a term can mean a person whose employment was terminated.
distinctions: The preserved noun denotes the person. Do not silently change it to the termination event or a fixed employment period.
usage: Informal workplace noun; interpret within its context.

originalSense.definition: One whose employment has been terminated

definition: A binding condition or promise in a contract or agreement.
example: The contract includes a term requiring written notice.
distinctions: A term is one condition or promise. A clause is a section of the written contract, which may contain more than one condition.

originalSense.definition: Any of the binding conditions or promises in a contract or agreement.

distinctionTask.prompt: The contract contains a _____ requiring written notice.
distinctionTask.explanation: This is a binding contractual condition.

definition: The agreed price and conditions governing how and when payment must be made.
example: Our terms require payment within thirty days.
distinctions: Payment terms concern price, timing or payment method. A loan term is its duration, while on good terms concerns a relationship.

originalSense.definition: Specifically, the conditions in a legal contract that specify the price and also how and when payment must be made.

distinctionTask.prompt: The invoice says payment is due in thirty days. These are payment _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Payment terms specify how and when payment is required.

definition: A limited or defined period of time.
example: The loan has a term of five years.
distinctions: The duration may depend on the agreement. Term does not always mean a period of one universal fixed length.

originalSense.definition: A limited or defined timespan.

distinctionTask.prompt: A five-year loan has a _____ of five years.
distinctionTask.explanation: This term is the duration of the loan.

definition: A period of holding office, especially one of a specified length.
example: The mayor began a second term in office.
distinctions: A term counts the period of office; it is different from one decision, meeting or election campaign.

originalSense.definition: Duration of officeholding, or its limit; period in office of fixed length.

distinctionTask.prompt: The mayor began a second _____ in office.
distinctionTask.explanation: A term is a period of holding the office.

definition: A period during which a court sits or is open for judicial business.
example: The court’s autumn term begins in October.
distinctions: Court terms follow the relevant court’s calendar. They need not match school terms or a judge’s full period in office.

originalSense.definition: The time during which legal courts are open.

definition: (Historical Scottish legal usage) A customary day on which rent is payable.
example: In the 1911 Scottish tenancy account, Whitsunday and Martinmas are called the two legal terms for paying rent.
distinctions: Here terms names payment days, rather than the tenancy’s duration. The historical account distinguishes legal and agreed payment dates; it does not establish the date due under a current lease.
